resources.string: Understand when an effect enters and leaves composition
Cancel suspended work by changing a key or removing its owner
Register and release resources with DisposableEffect
Update values without restarting with rememberUpdatedState
Apply the rules to two fictional practical cases
Insert an effect, change its key and remove it. Compare the start, cancellation and cleanup events.
Direct user actions belong in onClick. Use an effect when composition or its keys should own asynchronous work or an external resource.
Changing the key cancels the previous work. Removing the effect cancels it too.
A new value, the same effect
Start delivery, then change the message during the wait. The effect delivers the latest value without restarting.
Register a listener, then change its key. The previous resource must be released before the new registration. Removing it releases the listener.
Runs a coroutine owned by composition. It is cancelled when a key changes or its owner leaves. Use it for suspending work.
Acquires an external resource and releases it in onDispose. Use it for listeners, observers and registered callbacks.
Updates a captured value or callback without making it a key or restarting long-lived work.

Direct user action? → onClick
Suspending work owned by UI? → LaunchedEffect
Register and release a resource? → DisposableEffect
New value without restarting? → rememberUpdatedState
A missing key can keep stale data. An unstable key restarts too much work. A key represents the identity that invalidates the effect.
A fictional event is recorded after the same screen remains in composition for two seconds. Changing screenId cancels the previous wait.
DisposableEffect registers an observer on the current LifecycleOwner and removes it when its owner leaves composition.
Run an experiment to see its events here.
